title: Detection of inert arrows by colour projections
statement: Use small quasicategories, coherent triangles and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and symmetric infinity operads and inert maps of [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition]. Put $S=N(\mathsf{Fin}_*)$ and let $q:Q\to S$ be a symmetric infinity operad. Let $v:a\to b$ lie over an inert pointed map $\alpha:\langle n\rangle\to\langle m\rangle$. Choose $q$-cocartesian colour projections $\pi_j:b\to b_j$ over $\rho_j:\langle m\rangle\to\langle1\rangle$, for $1\leq j\leq m$, and coherent composites $\pi_jv$. Then $v$ is $q$-cocartesian if and only if every $\pi_jv$ is $q$-cocartesian. In arity $m=0$ the right-hand condition is empty, so every edge over an inert map to $\langle0\rangle$ is $q$-cocartesian.

source.place: Higher Algebra (2017), Theorem 2.3.3.23(1), printed pp. 266-268; Converse condition (i), Remark 2.1.2.9 and Definition 2.1.1.10: detection of inert arrows by their output projections. Agent expansion of the proof; read online 2026-10-17, WANTED archive in report.md. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical result.

proof.text: Suppose $v$ is $q$-cocartesian. Each $\pi_j$ is $q$-cocartesian by hypothesis, so the composition assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality] makes $\pi_jv$ $q$-cocartesian. This applies to any of the specified coherent composites: its assertion concerns a $2$-simplex, not a strictly associative choice of composition.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10; cocartesian composition for the forward implication

proof.text: Conversely assume that all $\pi_jv$ are $q$-cocartesian. Since $\alpha$ is inert, the operad axiom in [lem-coef-symmetric-operadic-fibration-recognition] supplies a $q$-cocartesian lift $u:a\to c$ of $\alpha$. Apply the defining cocartesian lifting property of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] to $\Lambda^2_0$: the given edges are $u:a\to c$ and $v:a\to b$, and the base triangle has edges $\alpha,\mathrm{id}_{\langle m\rangle},\alpha$. Its filler gives $h:c\to b$ in the strict fiber $Q_{\langle m\rangle}$ and a triangle $hu\simeq v$. This uses no lifting over active maps.

source.place: Remark 2.1.2.9, comparison from a chosen inert lift; expand its construction by the cocartesian outer horn

proof.text: Choose cocartesian projections $\kappa_j:c\to c_j$. Their transports and the prescribed $\pi_j:b\to b_j$ give the Segal functor $T:Q_{\langle m\rangle}\to Q_{\langle1\rangle}^{m}$. To specify its action coherently, let $I_m$ be the ordinary category with objects $o,1,\ldots,m$ and only nonidentity arrows $o\to j$, and map its nerve to $S$ by $o\mapsto\langle m\rangle$, $j\mapsto\langle1\rangle$ and $o\to j\mapsto\rho_j$. The pullback of $q$ is a cocartesian fibration: inner lifting is inherited degreewise; a globally cocartesian lift of a cone leg remains cocartesian in the pullback, because its outer-horn filler pairs with the prescribed base simplex. Identity edges have degenerate cocartesian lifts by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Straightening [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] therefore supplies the transport functors with all coherences, and hence edges $h_j=T_j(h):c_j\to b_j$ over $\mathrm{id}_{\langle1\rangle}$ and coherent squares $h_j\kappa_j\simeq\pi_jh$. The chosen lifts can represent this transport, with the contractible classification choices allowed by the straightening statement. The operad Segal axiom says exactly that $T$ is a functor equivalence.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10 and Remark 2.1.1.14; coherent colour transport used in Remark 2.1.2.9

proof.text: Put $u_j=\kappa_ju:a\to c_j$. Cocartesian composition makes $u_j$ cocartesian. Both $u_j$ and $\pi_jv$ lie over the same map $\rho_j\alpha$; the latter is cocartesian by the converse hypothesis. The triangle of step 2 and the transport square of step 3 give $h_ju_j\simeq\pi_jv$, including its compatibility over the base triangle. Composition and its associativity here are the coherent mapping composition of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Thus $h_j$ with this triangle is a morphism from $u_j$ to $\pi_jv$ in $L(a,\rho_j\alpha)$ of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-composition-initiality]. Both objects are initial by that node. Its comparison assertion says that forgetting this morphism's triangle yields an equivalence of targets in $Q_{\langle1\rangle}$. This underlying morphism is $h_j$, so every component of $T(h)$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Remark 2.1.2.9 and Theorem 2.3.3.23(1), converse; compare the two cocartesian lifts of each projected inert map

proof.text: The tuple of inverse edges for the $h_j$, with the tuples of their two inverse triangles, is an inverse for $T(h)$ in the degreewise product quasicategory. Let $U$ be a quasi-inverse to the Segal functor $T$ and $\eta:UT\simeq\mathrm{id}$. Functors preserve inverse triangles, so $UT(h)$ is an equivalence. Naturality gives $[h]=[\eta_b][UT(h)][\eta_c]^{-1}$ in the homotopy category of $Q_{\langle m\rangle}$. The mapping-composition node identifies invertible component classes with equivalence edges, so $h$ is an equivalence in this fiber. This is an explicit inverse calculation from the definitions of product and functor equivalence.

source.place: Remark 2.1.1.14 and Remark 2.1.2.9; elementary reflection of equivalences by the specified Segal equivalence

proof.text: The inverse of $h$ in the fiber is also an inverse in $Q$. For every $z\in Q$, precomposition by $h$ on mapping spaces is a homotopy equivalence: precomposition by its inverse is a homotopy inverse by the associativity, unit laws and inverse triangles in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. In the square of [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], the bottom map for $h$ is the identity, since $q(h)=\mathrm{id}_{\langle m\rangle}$. Such a square with an equivalence on top is a homotopy pullback: the path pullback along an identity retracts onto the other object by sending a path $\gamma$ starting at the specified image to $t\mapsto\gamma(st)$, with $s$ decreasing from $1$ to $0$; its free endpoint moves to that image. Hence the criterion makes $h$ $q$-cocartesian. Cocartesian composition in the triangle $hu\simeq v$ now makes $v$ $q$-cocartesian.

source.place: Remark 2.1.2.9; conclude from the equivalence comparison and cocartesian composition

proof.text: If $m=0$, the Segal equivalence in step 3 is $Q_{\langle0\rangle}\simeq\Delta^0$. There are no $j$ in step 4. In step 5 the tuple and both inverse triangles are the unique ones in the empty product, so $T(h)$ is an equivalence and the same quasi-inverse calculation proves that $h$ is an equivalence. Steps 2 and 6 still apply to the unique inert pointed map $\langle n\rangle\to\langle0\rangle$, including $n=0$. If $n=0<m$ there is no inert $\alpha$, since an output would have no preimage. When $n=m=1$ the calculation is just comparison with one projection. Thus the proof neither assumes a nonempty output family nor introduces a nonexistent projection.

source.place: Definition 2.1.1.10 and Remark 2.1.1.14; explicit nullary and smallest-arity checks

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q26-fe050ae5a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Pass with no changes; fixes/ is empty. Sources: HA is not archived and the report carries a WANTED line for it, so I fetched the public PDF and read Def. 2.1.1.10, Rem. 2.1.1.14, Rem. 2.1.2.9 and the proof of Thm 2.3.3.23(1)(a). The proof follows Rem. 2.1.2.9 exactly: compare v with a cocartesian lift of the inert map, then check each colour projection of the comparison. In the proof of 2.3.3.23(1)(a), the reduction to 'each F0(C)->F0(Ci) is inert' is the parent's use in its step 11. Small cases of the statement: for m=0 the fibre over <0> is a point, since the recognition node takes the empty product to be terminal, so the arity-zero clause is true. For n=0<m no inert map exists. n=m=1 and the ordinary coloured-operad nerve both agree with the statement. Steps: in step 1 the composition node is applied with the first edge v cocartesian, the right way round. Step 2 fills the outer horn of dimension 2 with u on edge 01 over the degenerate triangle (alpha, id, alpha), so h lies in the strict fibre. In step 3 the pullback over N(I_m) is a cocartesian fibration, and straightening supplies the colour transports with the chosen lifts, within its contractible choices; I accept this use of 'transport'. Step 4 uses the comparison clause of the initiality statement for two initial cocartesian lifts over rho_j alpha; the clause is in the statement, not borrowed from the node's proof. Step 5 is elementary: an equivalence is reflected through the quasi-inverse. In step 6 the mapping spaces of N(Fin_*) are discrete, so the bottom map of the criterion square is literally the identity; the criterion then makes h cocartesian, and composition makes v cocartesian. Step 7 handles the arity cases correctly. All citations are in unit sk-prop-sf-biduality-general apart from definitions, so no tool_uses are needed. No new nodes and no SGA source. The nearest 'inert' nodes in the DAG are not duplicates. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The statement is not weakened.
